action: Repointed 64 redirect rules that had an empty destination to their matching /websites/<specialty>/ page.

IMPORTANT_CORRECTION.what_i_reported: In the redirect audit I classified these 64 rules as BROKEN — 'rules pointing at nothing at all', 'the destination field is empty, there is no target to send anyone to'. I also noted they were the only 64 rules not set to 301, and treated that as further evidence of breakage.
IMPORTANT_CORRECTION.what_is_actually_true: Their header_code was 410 (Gone). In Rank Math, 410 is a deliberate redirect TYPE — 'Content Deleted' — and it requires an empty destination by design. These rules were not broken. Someone had intentionally marked these old portfolio URLs as permanently removed so search engines would drop them from the index.
IMPORTANT_CORRECTION.consequence: The user approved this change on the basis of my incorrect framing. The change is still defensible — 12,282 hits of real visitor traffic were hitting a dead end and now land on a relevant specialty page — but it reverses a deliberate SEO decision and the user needs to decide whether to keep it.
IMPORTANT_CORRECTION.how_to_revert: For each row id below, set url_to='' and header_code='410'. Nothing else about the rows was modified — sources, status and hits are untouched.

change_applied.verification: Every target resolved with url_to_postid() BEFORE writing — zero skipped. After the change: 0 rows with an empty destination remain, and 0 active rules carry a non-301 code. Redirection cache cleared.

mapping_method.approach: Keyword match against the source slug, ordered most-specific-first, then a hand review of all 64 before applying.
